claim: A read replica in a different AWS Region is used to improve disaster recovery, to scale reads into a Region closer to users, and to make migration between Regions easier.
question: Why create an RDS read replica in another AWS Region?

evidence.quote: Scale read operations into an AWS Region closer to your users.
Make it easier to migrate from a data center in one AWS Region to a data center in another AWS Region.

claim: A read replica in a different Region than its source can be expected to have more replication lag, because of the longer network channels between Regional data centers.
question: Why do cross-Region read replicas lag more than same-Region replicas?

values.display: longer network channels between regional data centers

evidence.quote: You can expect to see a higher level of lag time for any read replica that is in a different AWS Region than the source instance. This lag time comes from the longer network channels between regional data centers.

claim: A cross-Region read replica uses the default security group, and in most cases the default DB parameter group and option group of its engine.
question: Which security group and parameter group does a cross-Region read replica get?

values.display: The read replica uses the default security group.
default DB parameter group and DB option group

qualifiers.condition: Db2 needs a custom parameter group; MySQL and Oracle accept one through the CLI

evidence.quote: The read replica uses the default security group.
In most cases, the read replica uses the default DB parameter group and DB option group for the specified DB engine.

claim: When the source of a cross-Region read replica is deleted, the replica is promoted for Db2, MariaDB, SQL Server, MySQL and Oracle; for PostgreSQL its replication status becomes terminated and it is not promoted.
question: What happens to a cross-Region read replica when its source DB instance is deleted?

evidence.quote: For Db2, MariaDB, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and Oracle DB instances, when the source DB instance for a cross-Region read replica is deleted, the read replica is promoted.

For PostgreSQL DB instances, when the source DB instance for a cross-Region read replica is deleted, the replication status of the read replica is set to `terminated`. The read replica isn't promoted.

claim: You can replicate between the GovCloud (US-East) and GovCloud (US-West) Regions, but not into or out of GovCloud (US).
question: Can an RDS read replica cross into or out of AWS GovCloud (US)?

values.display: not into or out of GovCloud (US)

evidence.quote: You can replicate between the GovCloud (US-East) and GovCloud (US-West) Regions, but not into or out of GovCloud (US).

claim: Data transferred for cross-Region replication incurs RDS data transfer charges: the initial snapshot transfer and every data modification sent from the source Region to the replica Region.
question: Is cross-Region read replica replication traffic charged?

values.display: incurs Amazon RDS data transfer charges
data transferred out of the source AWS Region

claim: For MySQL and MariaDB you can reduce cross-Region data transfer costs by creating one replica from the source in the other Region and creating the other replicas there from that first replica.
question: How can you cut data transfer cost when you need several MySQL read replicas in another Region?

values.display: reducing the number of cross-Region read replicas

qualifiers.scope: RDS for MySQL and RDS for MariaDB

evidence.quote: For MySQL and MariaDB instances, you can reduce your data transfer costs by reducing the number of cross-Region read replicas that you create.
In this case, you create only one of the read replicas from the source DB instance. You create the other two replicas from the first read replica instead of the source DB instance.
